Rashi on Yevamot 40a:12:1.english: He is like one, etc. - And he has not lost his share in his brother's property.

Rashi on Yevamot 40a:12:2.english: He acquires the brother's property - And even if he divorces her the next day.

Rashi on Yevamot 40a:13:1.english: [It is] obvious - That he did not lose his right [to inherit].

Rashi on Yevamot 40a:13:2.hebrew: מהו דתימא - כלומר, לאו לאשמועינן דלא איבד זכותו תניא לה, אלא לאשמועינן דלא שקיל כולהו נכסי:
Rashi on Yevamot 40a:13:2.english: What might you have said - That is to say, it was not taught to teach us that he did not lose his right, but rather to teach us that he does not take all the property.

Rashi on Yevamot 40a:14:1.hebrew: אי הכי - דלגרועי אתא, הוה ליה למיתני אינו אלא כאחד כו':
Rashi on Yevamot 40a:14:1.english: If so - that [the Mishnah] comes to diminish [his rights], it should have taught: "He is only like one [of the brothers]," etc.

Rashi on Yevamot 40a:15:1.hebrew: ה"ג אלא סלקא דעתך אמינא ליקנסיה הואיל ואפסדה מייבום - שפסלה על האחין:
Rashi on Yevamot 40a:15:1.english: This is the reading: Rather, it could enter your mind to say [that] we should penalize him, since he caused her to forfeit levirate marriage - For he disqualified her from [marrying] the [other] brothers.

Rashi on Yevamot 40a:1:1.hebrew: שבתחלה - קודם שהוקדשה מנחה זו, היתה עליו בכלל היתר:
Rashi on Yevamot 40a:1:1.english: As initially - Before this meal-offering was consecrated, it was in the category of [what is] permitted to him.

Rashi on Yevamot 40a:1:2.hebrew: ונאסרה - כשהוקדשה, וחזרה והותרה בהקטרת הקומץ:
Rashi on Yevamot 40a:1:2.english: And it became forbidden - when it was consecrated, and it reverted and became permitted upon the burning of the handful.

Rashi on Yevamot 40a:1:3.english: One might [have thought] it would revert, etc. - As [the Gemara] explains [below].

Rashi on Yevamot 40a:20:1.hebrew: אף האי נמי - לאחר מיתת האב, אם מת האב לאחר יבומו של זה, מודה ר"י דנוטל זה חלקו וחלק אחיו:
Rashi on Yevamot 40a:20:1.english: So too, this one as well - after the death of the father: if the father died after this one's levirate marriage, Rabbi Yehuda concedes that this one takes his [own] portion and his brother's portion.

Rashi on Yevamot 40a:21:1.hebrew: על שם אחיו כתיב ולא על שם אביו - כתיב. וכיון דבשעה שקם על שם אחיו לא שקל, תו לא שקיל [דאי שקיל השתא, לא מנכסי אחיו שקיל אלא מנכסי אביו, דהא ירתינהו]:
Rashi on Yevamot 40a:21:1.english: “In the name of his brother” is written, and not “in the name of his father” - [so] it is written. And since at the time he arose in the name of his brother he did not take [any inheritance], he no longer takes [it] (for if he takes now, he does not take from his brother's property, but rather from his father's property, since they have inherited it).

Rashi on Yevamot 40a:22:1.hebrew: היכא דאיכא אב דלא שקיל - יבם נחלה, לא תתקיים מצות יבום:
Rashi on Yevamot 40a:22:1.english: Where there is a father, that [he] does not take - [i.e., the] yavam [does not take] the inheritance, the mitzva of yibum is not fulfilled.

Rashi on Yevamot 40a:26:1.hebrew: איסמייה - לכולה מתני', דמשנה שאינה צריכה היא:
Rashi on Yevamot 40a:26:1.english: Shall I remove it - [Shall I remove] the entire baraita, for it is an unnecessary teaching.

Rashi on Yevamot 40a:26:2.hebrew: אמר ליה לא - תסמייה, דאת "הלכה כרבי יהודה" אתנייך, ומשנה צריכה הואי:
Rashi on Yevamot 40a:26:2.english: He said to him: No - [do not] remove it, for you were taught "the halakha is like Rabbi Yehuda," and [thus] it was a necessary teaching.

Rashi on Yevamot 40a:26:3.hebrew: ומיקשה הוא דקשיא לך - היכי שביק רבנן ועביד כרבי יהודה? ואפכת לה, ושפיר עבדת דאפכת לה:
Rashi on Yevamot 40a:26:3.english: And it was a difficulty that was hard for you - How could [one] leave the Rabbis and act in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda? And you reversed it, and you did well that you reversed it.

Rashi on Yevamot 40a:27:1.hebrew: אסור בקרובותיה - כאילו היא אשתו, וכל קרובות הנאסרות מחמת אשה גמורה אסורות מדרבנן בחלוצה:
Rashi on Yevamot 40a:27:1.english: He is forbidden [to marry] her relatives - As though she were his wife, and all relatives who are forbidden on account of a full-fledged wife are forbidden by rabbinic decree in the case of a chalutzah.

Rashi on Yevamot 40a:2:1.english: Granted, according to Rava, who said it is [the opinion of] the Rabbis - and [it] teaches "a mitzvah," and does not teach "for a mitzvah."

Rashi on Yevamot 40a:3:1.hebrew: ה"ק כו' ואכלו אותם - את הקדשים אשר כופר בהם, כי היכי דתהוי כפרה שלימה:
Rashi on Yevamot 40a:3:1.english: This is what [the baraita] is saying, etc. And they shall eat them - [meaning,] the consecrated offerings through which atonement is attained, so that there will be complete atonement.

Rashi on Yevamot 40a:4:1.english: [If] he wishes, he - The priest who performed its service.

Rashi on Yevamot 40a:5:1.english: However, according to Rav Yitzḥak - who taught [that it refers] to [the proper manner of] the mitzvah, and [that] it is [the view of] Abba Shaul.

Rashi on Yevamot 40a:5:2.hebrew: הכא מאי תרי גווני איכא - דקא ממעט תנא: יכול תחזור להיתירה הראשון, ת"ל דלא? והא ליכא למימר תחזור להיתירה הראשון: רצה — לשם מצוה אוכלה, רצה — שלא לשם מצוה אוכלה, ת"ל דלא; דהא כל כמה דבעי ליכלה! דהתם הוא כי בעיל שלא לשם מצוה, פגע בערוה; אבל הכא, מאי קעביד? וע"כ בתרי גווני בעיא לאוקמי, דומיא דרישא:
Rashi on Yevamot 40a:5:2.english: Here, what two manners are there - that the Tanna excludes [one of them, saying]: "One might think it returns to its original permitted state; the verse teaches [that it does] not"? For one cannot say [that] "it returns to its original permitted state" [means]: if he wishes, he may eat it for the sake of the mitzva, [and] if he wishes, he may eat it not for the sake of the mitzva; the verse teaches [that he may] not — since however he wishes, let him eat it! For it is [only] there [in the case of levirate marriage] that when he engages in intercourse not for the sake of the mitzva, he encounters a forbidden relative; but here, what [wrong] is he doing? Yet perforce you must establish [this clause] as [referring to] two manners, similar to the first clause.

Rashi on Yevamot 40a:6:1.hebrew: אכילה גסה מי מקריא אכילה והאמר ר"ל כו' - וכיון דלאו אכילה היא, מואכלו אהרן ובניו דרישא נפקא:
Rashi on Yevamot 40a:6:1.english: Is excessive eating called eating? Didn't Reish Lakish say, etc. - And since it is not [considered] eating, it is derived from "and Aaron and his sons shall eat" [in] the first clause.

Rashi on Yevamot 40a:6:2.hebrew: פטור - דלא עבר על אשר לא תעונה, שאף זה עינוי הוא, שמזיק את עצמו:
Rashi on Yevamot 40a:6:2.english: He is exempt - For he has not transgressed "that shall not be afflicted," since this too is an affliction, as he harms himself.

Rashi on Yevamot 40a:7:1.hebrew: אלא - תרי גווני. הכי תיבעי למימר: רצה מצה אוכלה, רצה חמץ אוכלה, ת"ל "מצות תאכל" — ולא חמץ:
Rashi on Yevamot 40a:7:1.english: Rather - [There are] two manners [of preparing it]. Thus you should say: "[If] he wishes, he eats it unleavened; [if] he wishes, he eats it leavened," [whereupon] Scripture teaches: "It shall be eaten unleavened" — and not leavened.

Rashi on Yevamot 40a:8:1.hebrew: לא תאפה חמץ חלקם נתתי אותה - להכי סמיך חלקם ללא תאפה חמץ, לומר אפי' שירי מנחה שהם חלקם של כהנים לא תאפה חמץ, ומהתם נפקא:
Rashi on Yevamot 40a:8:1.english: It shall not be baked leavened; [as] their portion I have given it - For this reason [Scripture] juxtaposed "their portion" to "it shall not be baked leavened," to say [that] even the remainder of the meal-offering, which is the priests' portion, shall not be baked leavened; and from there it is derived.

Rashi on Yevamot 40a:8:3.hebrew: רצה חלוט אוכלה - ת"ל "מצות", ולא חלוט:
Rashi on Yevamot 40a:8:3.english: [If] he wishes, he may eat it boiled - [Therefore] the verse states "unleavened," and not boiled.

Rashi on Yevamot 40a:9:1.english: If it is unleavened, it is unleavened - And how is it excluded from the implication of "unleavened [it] shall be eaten"?

Rashi on Yevamot 40a:9:2.hebrew: ואי לאו מצה היא מצות אמר רחמנא - בשירי מנחת חובה, דכתיב בצו את אהרן "ואכלוה מצות", וה"ה לשאר מנחות; ולמה לי "מצות תאכל":
Rashi on Yevamot 40a:9:2.english: And if it is not unleavened, the Merciful One said “unleavened” - [This is stated] regarding the remnants of an obligatory meal-offering, as it is written in [Parashat] Tzav et Aharon, “and eat it unleavened,” and the same applies to other meal-offerings; and why do I need [the verse] “it shall be eaten unleavened”?

Tosafot on Yevamot 40a:10:1.hebrew: שנה בה קרא לעכב - הך דהכא לא הוי כמו "שנה עליו הכתוב לעכב" דעלמא, דמהיכא תיתי לעכב, דדלמא למצוה הוא דאמר רחמנא דלא ליעבד חלוט? אלא "לעכב" — כלומר: דבעינן מצה מעלייתא ולא חלוט:
Tosafot on Yevamot 40a:10:1.english: The verse repeated it to make it indispensable - This [instance] here is not like [the standard principle of] "the verse repeated it to make it indispensable" [used] elsewhere — for from where would it even arise [to say it is] indispensable, [as if] perhaps it was [only] as a mitzvah that the Merciful One said not to make boiled [dough]? Rather, "to make it indispensable" means to say that we require proper matzah, and not boiled [dough].

Tosafot on Yevamot 40a:11:1.hebrew: כיון דהדר אפייה בתנור - או באילפס, לחם איקרי, ואדם יוצא בה ידי חובתו בפסח. והא דאמר בפ' כל שעה (פסחים דף לו:): "לחם עוני — פרט לחלוט ואשישה", אר"ת דהתם בלא הדר אפייה בתנור. ועוד אר"ת: דהתם בחלוט גדול דומיא דאשישה, ולא חשיב לחם עוני לפי שהוא גדול, ולא משום דחלוט. א"נ: התם בבלילתו קשה, והכא בבלילתו רכה, כגון סופגנין או חלת המשרת, דמפרש התם דהיינו חלוט של בעלי בתים, דלא מחייב בחלה ולא חשיב לחם אלא על ידי אפיה, ולהכי חשיב שפיר לחם עוני אע"ג דחלטיה; אבל בלילתו עבה מיפסל לעשות, דחשיב לחם עשירות אפי' לא הדר אפייה. ובפ' כל שעה (שם ד"ה פרט) הארכתי:
Tosafot on Yevamot 40a:11:1.english: Since he subsequently baked it in an oven - Or in a pan [ilpas], it is called bread, and a person fulfills his obligation with it on Passover. And [as for] that which [the Gemara] says in chapter Kol Sha'ah (Pesachim 36b): "'Bread of affliction' — excluding scalded dough [chalut] and a large pancake [ashishah]," Rabbeinu Tam said that there [it refers to a case] where he did not subsequently bake it in an oven. And furthermore, Rabbeinu Tam said that there [it refers to] a large chalut, similar to an ashishah, and it is not considered "bread of affliction" because it is large, and not because it is chalut. Alternatively: there [it refers to a case] where its batter is thick, whereas here [it refers to a case] where its batter is loose, such as sufganin [sponge cakes] or challat hamisret [pan-fried dough], which [the Gemara] explains there to be the chalut of householders, which is not obligated in challah and is only considered bread through baking; and therefore it is properly considered "bread of affliction" even though he scalded it. However, [when] its batter is thick, it is disqualified from being used [for matzah], since it is considered "rich bread" even if he did not subsequently bake it. And in chapter Kol Sha'ah (ibid., s.v. Perat), I have elaborated.

Tosafot on Yevamot 40a:4:1.hebrew: רצה כהן אחר אוכלה - והא דדרשינן בפ"ב דקדושין (דף נג.): "לכל בני אהרן תהיה איש כאחיו" — היינו של אותו משמר או של אותו בית אב. א"נ, הכא מרבוי ילפינן דכהן המקריב צריך שיאכל ממנה, ולא כולה:
Tosafot on Yevamot 40a:4:1.english: "[If] he wishes, another priest may eat it" - And [regarding] that which we expound in the second chapter of Kiddushin (53a): "[It shall belong] to all the sons of Aaron, each man like his brother" (Leviticus 7:10) — that refers to [priests] of that watch or of that father's house. Alternatively, here we learn from a [scriptural] amplification that the priest who offers [it] must eat from it, and not [necessarily] all of it.

Tosafot on Yevamot 40a:5:1.hebrew: מאי תרי גווני איכא - דליכא למימר: רצה לשם סעודה אוכלה, רצה לשם מצוה; דאין צריך שיתכוין לשם מצוה, אלא שלא יהא אוכלה אכילה גסה:
Tosafot on Yevamot 40a:5:1.english: What two manners are there? - For one cannot say [that the two manners are:] if he wishes, he eats it for the sake of a meal, [and] if he wishes, for the sake of a mitzvah; for he does not need to have intention for the sake of a mitzvah, rather [only] that he should not eat it as excessive eating.

Tosafot on Yevamot 40a:6:1.hebrew: אכילה גסה ביוה"כ פטור - וא"ת, דאמר בפרק מי שאמר הריני נזיר (נזיר דף כג. ושם): "כי ישרים דרכי ה', צדיקים ילכו בם ופושעים יכשלו בם" (הושע י״ד:י׳), משל לב' בני אדם שצלו פסחיהן, אחד אכלו לשם פסחו ואחד אכלו אכילה גסה; ומשמע התם דתרוייהו נפקי, אלמא הויא אכילה? וי"ל, דתרי עניני אכילה גסה הם:
Tosafot on Yevamot 40a:6:1.english: "Excessive eating on Yom Kippur, one is exempt" - And if you will ask: Doesn't [the Gemara] say in the chapter [entitled] Mi She'amar Hareini Nazir (Nazir 23a and there [elsewhere]): "For the ways of the Lord are upright; the righteous will walk in them, and the wicked will stumble in them" (Hosea 14:10) — a parable of two people who roasted their Paschal offerings: one ate it for the sake of his Paschal offering [mitzvah], and one ate it [as] excessive eating; and it is implied there that both fulfilled [their obligation], thus it is [considered] eating? And one can answer that there are two types of excessive eating.

Tosafot on Yevamot 40a:9:1.hebrew: מצות אמר רחמנא - פי' בקונט': "ואכלוה מצות אצל המזבח" וגו', ובשמיני של מלואים כתיב. ואפילו לשמואל דאמר בריש הקומץ רבה (מנחות דף יט:) דלא ילפינן דורות משעה — שמא הכא איכא שום יתור:
Tosafot on Yevamot 40a:9:1.english: The Merciful One states "unleavened" - Rashi explained: [This refers to the verse,] "And eat it unleavened beside the altar, etc." (Leviticus 10:12), which is written regarding the eighth day of the inauguration [of the Tabernacle]. And even according to Shmuel, who says at the beginning of [chapter] HaKometz Rabbah (Menachot 19b) that we do not derive [laws for] future generations from a temporary [ruling] — perhaps here there is some superfluous [wording].
